tasks.details:

• In ModelDescription.F90 (ReadMaterial):

       CALL LoadSimplifiedMaterial(libId,Mat)
   END IF
• Implement `LoadSimplifiedMaterial` in new Fortran module MaterialLib.F90 reading /usr/src/elmerfem/work/materials.json (use Fortran 2008 intrinsic ISO_FORTRAN_ENV + simple JSON parser e.g. FSON).
• Re-compile inside Dockerfile (add `git clone https://github.com/juntsang/FSON` && make install).

<info added on 2025-07-23T21:31:02.355Z>
**UPDATE based on research:** The initial plan to modify `Types.F90` is incorrect and should be avoided. The existing flexible `ValueList_t` structure is sufficient and safer. The implementation should proceed as follows:
• **No changes to `Types.F90`**. The `hasSimplifiedId` and `libId` fields are not needed in the core data structure.
• In `ModelDescription.F90`'s `ReadMaterial`, the call should be to `LoadSimplifiedMaterial(LibId, Mat % Values)`.
• The new `LoadSimplifiedMaterial` subroutine in `MaterialLib.F90` must map the JSON keys from `materials.json` to the standard Elmer SIF keywords using `ListAddReal`:
   - `E` -> `'Youngs Modulus'`
   - `nu` -> `'Poissons Ratio'`
   - `rho` -> `'Density'`
   - `k` -> `'Heat Conductivity'`
</info added on 2025-07-23T21:31:02.355Z>

<info added on 2025-07-23T21:32:39.730Z>
• **Research Finding:** The primary target for instrumentation is the main **Sweep Loop** in `ElmerSolver.F90`.
• This `DO WHILE (.TRUE.)` loop uses `iSweep` as the current iteration counter and `OptimIters` as the total number of iterations.
• The relevant code block is:
  ```fortran
  DO WHILE (.TRUE.)
    iSweep = iSweep + 1
    ...
    CALL ExecSimulation(...)
    ...
    IF (iSweep == OptimIters) EXIT
  END DO
  ```
• The more granular time-stepping and nonlinear iteration loops are encapsulated within the `ExecSimulation` subroutine. Instrumenting these for the `<timeStep>/<total>` part of the progress format will require deeper analysis of that subroutine.
